newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks plunge on unexpected poll result.
newsitem.headline: French stocks plunge on unexpected poll result.

text.p: French shares plunged on Monday morning after a strong lead by the opposition left-wing parties in the first round of a parliamentary election on Sunday against expectations the governing centre-right coalition would win.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index opened down 106.03 points or 3.84 percent at 2,656.87 while the CAC-40 May futures contract was down at 2,670 from 2,761 at Friday's close.
The CAC-40 index was down 4.13 percent after five minutes of trading.

With most votes counted in metropolitan France, the Interior Ministry said the combined left had polled 40.1 percent, the RPR-UDF coalition and other right-wing candidates 36.5 percent and the National Front 15 percent. Ecologists scored 6.8 percent.
Most of the 577 National Assembly seats are set to go to a run-off on June 1, where the behaviour of Front supporters and of the 31.6 percent of voters who abstained will be crucial.
Financial markets had been expecting the centre-right to hold on to a reduced majority. "The market is going to be volatile all week," said a trader.

"The stock market, putting its trust in opinion polls showing the right would win, had treated the election as a non-event. We are going to pay for it because the market had not taken the political risk fully into account," a dealer said.

"We are faced with the worst possible scenario. Is the right going to return the votes in their favour in the second round? If the left wins, what is going to happen to the Maastricht Treaty? And what about issues such as Thomson ?," another dealer said.
They added it was now necessary to protect one's money and sell even if the election result did not impact the fundamentals such as corporate results.
